issue_context.title: PEReader.GetPESectionBlock() cache ineffective (calls mmap+munmap for every call)
issue_context.body:
### Description

In https://github.com/icsharpcode/ILSpy/issues/2416, @tellowkrinkle observed unexpected significant disk I/O when decompiling with ilspycmd.
ilspycmd uses System.Reflection.Metadata to read the assembly being decompiled. Due to the caching bug described below, reading 14 MB of assemblies requires 6.5 GB of disk I/O.

### Configuration

@tellowkrinkle originally observed the problem on MacOS; but we've managed to reproduce it on Linux ubuntu 5.8.0-44-generic x86_64.
.NET runtime is version 3.1.15; but System.Reflection.Metadata.dll is used via NuGet in version 5.0.0.

### Data

strace shows a large number of syscalls:
```
mmap(NULL, 1143380, PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, 40, 0) = 0x7f5ab4554000
madvise(0x7f5ab4554000, 1143380, MADV_DONTFORK) = 0
msync(0x7f5ab4554000, 1142356, MS_SYNC|MS_INVALIDATE) = 0
munmap(0x7f5ab4554000, 1143380)         = 0
```
This sequence of syscalls seems to repeat once for each call to `System.Reflection.Metadata.PEReaderExtensions.GetMethodBody`.
The `msync` call seems to flush the disk cache -> every single call to `GetMethodBody` ends up performing disk I/O.

Setting a breakpoint on `msync` shows that it is called from the following stack:
```
(lldb) clrstack
OS Thread Id: 0x2044 (1)
        Child SP               IP Call Site
00007FFFFFFFA4D0 00007ffff7fa5960 [InlinedCallFrame: 00007fffffffa4d0] Interop+Sys.MSync(IntPtr, UInt64, MemoryMappedSyncFlags)
00007FFFFFFFA4D0 00007fff7e9b8683 [InlinedCallFrame: 00007fffffffa4d0] Interop+Sys.MSync(IntPtr, UInt64, MemoryMappedSyncFlags)
00007FFFFFFFA4C0 00007FFF7E9B8683 ILStubClass.IL_STUB_PInvoke(IntPtr, UInt64, MemoryMappedSyncFlags)
00007FFFFFFFA550 00007FFF7E5B9ACB System.IO.MemoryMappedFiles.MemoryMappedView.Flush(UIntPtr) [/_/src/System.IO.MemoryMappedFiles/src/System/IO/MemoryMappedFiles/MemoryMappedView.Unix.cs @ 147]
00007FFFFFFFA5A0 00007FFF7E5B9A24 System.IO.MemoryMappedFiles.MemoryMappedViewAccessor.Flush() [/_/src/System.IO.MemoryMappedFiles/src/System/IO/MemoryMappedFiles/MemoryMappedViewAccessor.cs @ 71]
00007FFFFFFFA5C0 00007FFF7E5B994C System.IO.MemoryMappedFiles.MemoryMappedViewAccessor.Dispose(Boolean) [/_/src/System.IO.MemoryMappedFiles/src/System/IO/MemoryMappedFiles/MemoryMappedViewAccessor.cs @ 41]
00007FFFFFFFA5F0 00007FFF7D830C5D System.IO.UnmanagedMemoryAccessor.Dispose() [/_/src/System.Private.CoreLib/shared/System/IO/UnmanagedMemoryAccessor.cs @ 120]
00007FFFFFFFA610 00007FFF7E9B7FB4 System.Reflection.Internal.MemoryMappedFileBlock+DisposableData.Release() [/_/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Metadata/src/System/Reflection/Internal/MemoryBlocks/MemoryMappedFileBlock.cs @ 49]
00007FFFFFFFA630 00007FFF7E9B7F04 System.Reflection.Internal.MemoryMappedFileBlock+DisposableData.Release()
00007FFFFFFFA670 00007FFF7E9B7DA0 System.Reflection.Internal.CriticalDisposableObject.Dispose() [/_/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Metadata/src/System/Reflection/Internal/Utilities/CriticalDisposableObject.cs @ 13]
00007FFFFFFFA690 00007FFF7E9B7C74 System.Reflection.Internal.MemoryMappedFileBlock.Dispose() [/_/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Metadata/src/System/Reflection/Internal/MemoryBlocks/MemoryMappedFileBlock.cs @ 67]
00007FFFFFFFA6B0 00007FFF7E9B7B63 System.Reflection.PortableExecutable.PEReader.GetPESectionBlock(Int32) [/_/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Metadata/src/System/Reflection/PortableExecutable/PEReader.cs @ 416]
00007FFFFFFFA760 00007FFF7E9B7850 System.Reflection.PortableExecutable.PEReader.GetSectionData(Int32) [/_/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Metadata/src/System/Reflection/PortableExecutable/PEReader.cs @ 485]
00007FFFFFFFA7F0 00007FFF7E9B76E8 System.Reflection.Metadata.PEReaderExtensions.GetMethodBody(System.Reflection.PortableExecutable.PEReader, Int32) [/_/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Metadata/src/System/Reflection/Metadata/PEReaderExtensions.cs @ 31]
00007FFFFFFFA8B0 00007FFF7E9B62A0 ICSharpCode.Decompiler.CSharp.CSharpDecompiler.ReadCodeMappingInfo(ICSharpCode.Decompiler.Metadata.PEFile, ICSharpCode.Decompiler.Metadata.CodeMappingInfo, System.Reflection.Metadata.MethodDefinitionHandle, System.Reflection.Metadata.MethodDefinitionHandle, System.Collections.Generic.Queue`1<System.Reflection.Metadata.MethodDefinitionHandle>, System.Collections.Generic.HashSet`1<System.Reflection.Metadata.TypeDefinitionHandle>) [/home/siegfried/ILSpy/ICSharpCode.Decompiler/CSharp/CSharpDecompiler.cs @ 673]
```

### Analysis

The caching logic in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/202c9fd3463ada7094762eb1274d948c5dd78bc7/src/libraries/System.Reflection.Metadata/src/System/Reflection/PortableExecutable/PEReader.cs#L377 is broken:
there is a "cache miss" code path that creates a new `AbstractMemoryBlock` and caches it; but there is no "cache hit" code path that returns the existing `AbstractMemoryBlock` without allocating a new one.
For each index only the first-created `AbstractMemoryBlock` is returned to the caller, but every additional call to `GetPESectionBlock` unnecessarily creates+disposes an additional `AbstractMemoryBlock`.
The code path commented as `// another thread created the block already, we need to dispose ours:` ends up running all the time, even in single-threaded code!
When `PEStreamOptions.PrefetchEntireImage` is not in use, this triggers additional syscalls.

Also, I don't see a good reason for calling `msync` at all, given that the file is mapped read-only.
comments: @dgrunwald do you feel like sending PR with the fix? Do you have a simpler repo perhaps which doesn't involve ilspycmd?

> The bug can be worked around by using `PEStreamOptions.PrefetchEntireImage`. This avoids the `msync` calls completely and reduces the run-time to 2.24s. I think the `msync` doesn't actually flush the disk cache on Linux (unlike what was reported on MacOS, which I can't test on) so the performance impact isn't as catastrophic.

Testing on MacOS, I got permission errors trying to open the file in place, so I copied it to `/tmp/` (and then to an SD card).
```
SSD     | PEStreamOptions.Default             |  2.2s
SSD     | PEStreamOptions.PrefetchEntireImage |  0.074s
SD Card | PEStreamOptions.Default             | 13.7s
SD Card | PEStreamOptions.PrefetchEntireImage |  0.09s
```
It seems there's a fair amount of overhead for `dotnet run` (vs `dotnet bin/.../thing.dll`), so the performance impact might seem a bit more catastrophic if you run it that way (which I did for the above numbers)
@dgrunwald @tellowkrinkle any chance you could try the proposed fix above and see the numbers? Would be nice to see the comparison run on the same machine.

review_comments: Could this new code go under an `else` for the `if` statement above?

I considered it, but there is a rare case where this code races with another thread and that thread is able to fill the cache.  By leaving this out of the else we give ourselves that small window to get a cache hit.
